title: GET /api/dashboard/metrics returns 200 success:true for an authenticated org member
steps: As an authenticated user with a valid orgId, call GET /api/dashboard/metrics
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with body { success: true, data: {...} }.

title: /dashboard renders without a console error or unhandled rejection on first load
automationRef: test-automation/tests/overview/overview-smoke.test.ts::tests 1, 14, 15 (test 15’s wait condition is stale — see description)
preconditions: Seeded demo org with at least one active project
steps: Navigate to /dashboard as an authenticated user
Monitor the browser console for the duration of the initial load
expectedResult: No JS console error or unhandled promise rejection is logged during load.
description: Test 15 in the referenced spec waits for the text 'Loading dashboard metrics...' to disappear before sampling console errors — that literal text no longer exists anywhere in the Dashboard 2.0 rewrite (the loading state is now Chakra Skeleton placeholders with no such string), so the wait resolves immediately rather than actually waiting for load completion. The spec still runs and its 'no console error' assertion is still meaningful, but it is weaker than intended and should be rewritten to wait for a real post-load signal (e.g. the module rail's skeleton rows disappearing).

title: All 7 module rail entries render with their correct icon and label on initial load
automationRef: test-automation/tests/overview/overview-smoke.test.ts (test 3 currently asserts exact-text "<X> Board" cards from the old grid, which don’t render in the new rail — only the short label does; needs rewriting against OverviewModuleRail’s markup)
steps: Navigate to /dashboard and wait for the rail’s loading skeletons to finish
expectedResult: All 7 rail entries appear in order (Summary, Audit, Risk, Resource, Framework, Compliance, Vendor) each with its correct icon and label.
description: Dashboard 2.0 rewrite (2026-08-13): there is no more idle grid. OverviewModuleRail permanently lists Summary (LayoutDashboard), Audit Board (ClipboardCheck), Risk Board (TrendingUp), Resource Board (ShieldAlert), Framework Board (Shield), Compliance Board (CheckCircle2), and Vendor Board (Building2) — 7 entries, not 6 — each shown with its icon and a label equal to board.title.replace(' Board', '') (so 'Summary' stays as-is, others drop the word 'Board').

title: DashboardFilterBar renders without throwing when filterOptions.frameworks is empty
description: A fresh org has no active frameworks yet, so filterOptions.frameworks arrives as []. SHOW_FRAMEWORKS_FILTER is currently false anyway, but the date-preset, severity, and project controls must still mount cleanly.
steps: Navigate to /dashboard for an org with zero active frameworks
expectedResult: The date preset, severity chips, and project picker all render and are interactive; no exception is thrown.

title: risk-distribution and risk-areas endpoints return 200 with an empty array when orgId can't be resolved
description: Both /api/dashboard/risk-distribution and /api/dashboard/risk-areas have an early-return path for a missing req.orgId, returning success:true with an empty distribution/services array rather than erroring.
steps: Call GET /api/dashboard/risk-distribution with a token that resolves no orgId
Call GET /api/dashboard/risk-areas under the same condition
expectedResult: Both return HTTP 200 with { success: true, data: { distribution: [] } } and { success: true, data: { services: [] } } respectively.

title: PriorityActionsPanel mounts and shows either populated chips or the explicit empty state, without throwing
steps: Navigate to /dashboard for any org (populated or fresh) and wait for the top strip to finish loading
expectedResult: The Priority Actions strip renders either at least one severity-colored chip or the 'All clear — nothing urgent in the last 7 days.' text — never a blank area, a spinner stuck indefinitely, or a thrown error.

title: DashboardFilterBar's Filters popover opens/closes cleanly and its merged Projects picker lists the org's real projects
description: DashboardFilterBar now owns project scope directly (the former standalone top-right ProjectsDropdown was merged into its Filters popover) alongside date/severity/framework controls.
steps: Open the Projects dropdown inside the panel
expectedResult: The Filters popover opens without error; the Projects dropdown lists every one of the org's real projects by name (not empty, not a loading spinner stuck indefinitely); closing the popover leaves the dashboard in a usable state.
